claims.claim: Tesla said the function of the buried machinery was "to have a grip on the earth so the whole of this globe can quiver"
claims.quote: In Tesla's words, the function of this was "to have a grip on the earth so the whole of this globe can quiver".

claims.claim: Tesla doubted radio waves (Hertzian waves) existed
claims.quote: Tesla discarded the idea of using the newly discovered Hertzian waves (radio waves), detected in 1888 by German physicist Heinrich Rudolf Hertz. Tesla doubted they existed

claims.claim: Tesla believed Hertzian waves, if they existed, would travel straight out into space and be "hopelessly lost"
claims.quote: meaning they would travel straight out into space and be "hopelessly lost"

claims.claim: Tesla theorized that current injected into the Earth at the right frequency would resonate in standing waves that could be tapped anywhere on the planet
claims.quote: He theorized from these experiments that if he injected electric current into the Earth at just the right frequency he could harness what he believed was the planet's own electrical charge and cause it to resonate at a frequency that would be amplified in "standing waves" that could be tapped anywhere on the planet to run devices or, through modulation, carry a signal.

claims.claim: Morgan agreed to give Tesla $150,000
claims.quote: Morgan signed a contract with Tesla in March 1901, agreeing to give the inventor $150,000 ($5.81 million in 2025) to develop and build a wireless station on Long Island

claims.claim: The March 1901 contract gave Morgan a 51% interest in the company and in the wireless patents
claims.quote: The deal also included Morgan having a 51% interest in the company as well as a 51% share in present and future wireless patents developed from the project.

claims.claim: In June 1901 Tesla read a Marconi article and afterwards decided to scale up to a far more powerful transmitter with wireless power delivery
claims.quote: Tesla's plans changed radically after he read a June 1901 Electrical Review article by Marconi titled "Syntonic Wireless Telegraph".

claims.claim: Tesla concluded Marconi was copying his earth-resonance system
claims.quote: the description of the Italian inventor's use of a "Tesla coil" "connected to the Earth" led Tesla to believe Marconi was copying his earth resonance system to do it

claims.claim: Morgan refused the additional money and demanded an account of money already spent
claims.quote: With Tesla basically proposing a breach of contract, Morgan refused to lend additional funds and demanded an account of money already spent.

claims.claim: The 1904 photograph was taken so Tesla could go back to J. P. Morgan to ask for additional funds
claims.quote: This 1904 photo of Wardenclyffe was taken so that Tesla could go back to J. P. Morgan to try and get the additional funds he needed to finish the tower.

claims.claim: Tesla's 1923 foreclosure testimony describes a wood and steel lined shaft sunk 120 feet beneath the tower with a stairway inside
claims.quote: The descriptions (some from Tesla's 1923 testimony in foreclosure proceedings on the property) include that the facility had a ten by twelve foot wood and steel lined shaft sunk into the ground 120 feet (37 m) beneath the tower with a stairway inside it.

claims.claim: Machines at the bottom of the shaft pushed sixteen iron pipes three hundred feet
claims.quote: "had special machines rigged up which would push the iron pipe, one length after another, and I pushed these iron pipes, I think sixteen of them, three hundred feet, and then the current through these pipes takes hold of the earth."

claims.claim: Four 100-foot tunnels are described radiating north, south, east and west, terminating in small brick igloos
claims.quote: There is also contemporaneous and later descriptions of four 100 foot long tunnels, possibly brick lined and waterproofed, radiating from the bottom of the shaft north, south, east, and west terminating back at ground level in little brick igloos.

claims.claim: Morgan's refusal letter came on July 14, 1903
claims.quote: Morgan's reply on July 14 was "I have received your letter and in reply would say that I should not feel disposed at present to make any further advances".

claims.claim: That night and several nights after, newspapers reported bright flashes from the tower lighting the sky
claims.quote: The night of Morgan's reply, and several nights after, newspapers reported that the Wardenclyffe tower came alive shooting off bright flashes lighting up the night sky.

claims.claim: Wardenclyffe never seemed to operate again after those nights
claims.quote: No explanation was forthcoming from Tesla or any of his workers as to the meaning of the display and Wardenclyffe never seemed to operate again.

claims.claim: In 1917 the Smiley Steel Company dynamited the tower and the scrap was worth $1,750
claims.quote: On July 4, 1917, the Smiley Steel Company of New York began demolition of the tower by dynamiting it. The tower was knocked on a tilt by the initial explosion but it was not totally demolished until September. The scrap value realized was $1,750 (equivalent to $44,000 in 2025).

claims.claim: It took until September to bring the tower down
claims.quote: The tower was knocked on a tilt by the initial explosion but it was not totally demolished until September.

claims.claim: How Tesla intended to combine ground conduction with the atmospheric method is unknown
claims.quote: How Tesla intended to employ the ground conduction method and atmospheric method in Wardenclyffe's design is unknown.

claims.claim: The purpose of the tunnels is only speculated: drainage, access, or enhancing ground connection or resonance
claims.quote: Speculation on the tunnels ranges from them being for drainage, acting as access ways, or having the function of enhancing ground connection or resonance by interacting with the water table below the tower

claims.claim: Tesla lit lamps wirelessly at Colorado Springs but never scientifically tested his Earth resonance theory
claims.quote: Although Tesla demonstrated wireless power transmission at Colorado Springs, lighting electric lights mounted outside the building where he had his large experimental coil, he did not scientifically test his theories.

claims.claim: Tesla believed he had achieved Earth resonance, which by his theory would work at any distance
claims.quote: He believed he had achieved Earth resonance which, according to his theory, would work at any distance.

claims.claim: The rumour that the US government destroyed the tower because of German spies was false
claims.quote: Since this was during World War I a rumor spread, picked up by newspapers and other publications, that the tower was demolished on orders of the United States Government with claims German spies were using it as a radio transmitter or observation post, or that it was being used as a landmark for German submarines.

claims.claim: Tesla could not reveal the real reason for the demolition because the mortgages and foreclosure had been kept off the public record
claims.quote: but since the original mortgages with Boldt as well as the foreclosure had been kept off the public record in order to hide his financial difficulties, Tesla was not able to reveal the real reason for the demolition

claims.claim: Tesla built the station at Shoreham, New York in 1901–1902
claims.quote: an early experimental wireless transmission station designed and built by scientist Nikola Tesla on Long Island in 1901–1902, located in the village of Shoreham, New York

claims.claim: The site was 200 acres bought from land developer James S. Warden
claims.quote: Tesla purchased 200 acres (81 ha) of land close to a railway line 65 miles (105 km) from New York City in Shoreham on Long Island Sound from land developer James S. Warden

claims.claim: Tesla intended to send messages, telephony and facsimile images across the Atlantic to England and to ships at sea
claims.quote: Tesla intended to transmit messages, telephony, and even facsimile images across the Atlantic Ocean to England and to ships at sea based on his theories of using the Earth to conduct the signals.

claims.claim: The tower was 186 feet tall
claims.quote: The Tesla biographer John Joseph O'Neill noted the cupola at the top of the 186-foot tower had a 5-foot hole in its top

claims.claim: The project was abandoned in 1906
claims.quote: Additional investment could not be found, and the project was abandoned in 1906, never to become operational.
